headline: Currencies are holding still before US inflation figures at 7:30 AM CT, the last big price check before the Federal Reserve's December 9 decision. Oil kept sliding, with Brent near $91, its lowest since late August.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: The dollar index held near 101.6 in Asian trading as markets waited for US inflation figures at 7:30 AM CT. Bets on a December Federal Reserve hike sit above four in five, so a hot reading matters more than a soft one.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: High oil from the US–Iran war has kept US inflation well above the Federal Reserve's 2% goal; the Fed raised rates in September and held on October 28, with two officials voting to hike. A strong October jobs report last Friday lifted the dollar, and on Monday it gave back about half of that as oil fell and stocks recovered. What changed: Little overnight. The dollar sat still in Asia, with traders unwilling to push it further down before the inflation figures. Rate markets put the chance of a December hike at roughly 80% to 85%. Oil slid again, which eases one source of US price pressure. What it means: The dollar now rests mostly on rate support rather than fear, so today's inflation reading is the main swing factor. A monthly rise of 0.3% or more would make a December hike look close to certain; a clearly soft reading would revive doubts. The question: how much pressure is the Fed under after today's figures?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up, all times CT: 3:00 AM, Fed governor Christopher Waller speaks; 7:30 AM, US consumer prices for October (forecast +0.3% on the month, core +0.2%; September was +0.6%); 12:00 PM, a 10-year Treasury bond sale. Wednesday is Veterans Day, so the US bond market is closed. Friday, 7:30 AM, US wholesale (producer) prices.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro held near $1.122 overnight, keeping Monday's gain as oil kept falling. European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde speaks twice this week, starting Wednesday.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Energy costs from the Iran war pushed euro-area inflation to about 4% in October, double the European Central Bank's goal, and markets expect the bank to raise its 2.50% deposit rate in December. Weak spending and France's debt worries pushed the euro to about $1.1105 last week, its lowest since May 2025. What changed: No euro-area news overnight. The euro held Monday's rise of about 0.6% as Brent crude slipped toward $91, its lowest since late August. What it means: Cheaper oil helps the euro because the region buys most of its fuel abroad, but the US still looks set to raise rates in December, so the rate gap keeps leaning toward the dollar. The question: do today's US inflation figures widen that gap?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up, all times CT: Tuesday, 7:30 AM, US inflation figures, which move the euro through the dollar side; Wednesday, 3:45 AM, and Thursday, 1:30 PM, ECB President Christine Lagarde speaks; Friday, 4:00 AM, the second estimate of euro-area third-quarter growth (the first was +0.4%). The next ECB decision is December 17.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: The pound held near $1.344, close to where it sat after the Bank of England's November 5 rate hike. UK growth figures for the third quarter come Thursday.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Energy and fuel costs pushed UK inflation to 3.5% in September, its highest in about a year. On November 5 the Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4.00%, its first hike since 2023, and Governor Andrew Bailey said it is unlikely to be the last unless the Middle East conflict is resolved. What changed: No UK news overnight; the pound was steady in Asia after gaining with most currencies on Monday. What it means: The pound is holding on the promise of another hike, but falling oil weakens that case a little each day it lasts. The question: does oil stay high enough to force another Bank of England hike?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up, all times CT: Tuesday, 7:30 AM, US inflation figures; Thursday, 1:00 AM, UK growth for the third quarter and for September (forecast +0.7% on the quarter, after +0.5%). UK jobs and pay figures follow on November 17, and the next Bank of England decision is December 17.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: The dollar held near 158 yen after Bank of Japan meeting notes showed several members want to raise rates faster. Markets had already expected a December hike, so the yen barely moved.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The yen has been weak for months because Japanese rates sit far below others. The Bank of Japan held at 1.25% on October 30, but markets expect a hike in December, and Japan spent about $97 billion in July and August buying yen to support it. What changed: The bank's summary of opinions from the October meeting showed several members want to raise rates without being overly cautious and to move faster toward a level that neither speeds up nor slows the economy, which one put well above 1%. Others warned that weak household spending argues for patience; spending fell 6.8% on a year earlier in September. What it means: The board is now debating how fast to hike, not whether, which backs December pricing. But that was largely expected, so the rate gap with the US still dominates. The question: does the December hike stay on track while US yields stay high?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up, all times CT: Tuesday, 7:30 AM, US inflation figures, the biggest risk for the dollar–yen rate; Wednesday, 5:50 PM, Japanese wholesale prices for October (forecast 6.5% on a year earlier). The next Bank of Japan decision is December 18.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The franc was steady near 0.820 per dollar and 0.920 per euro overnight. Calmer stock markets keep safe-haven demand low, and there is no Swiss news this week.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Swiss National Bank holds its rate at zero, and Swiss inflation rose to 1.5% in October on fuel prices, which makes another cut less likely. The franc tends to draw money when markets get nervous. What changed: Nothing Swiss. Stocks held their Monday rebound in Asia and oil kept falling on hopes of calm in the Gulf, so there was little reason to buy safe havens. What it means: The franc's pull depends on fear, and fear stays low for now. The central bank has said it can sell francs if they get too strong, so it is comfortable with a softer franc. The question: does the calm in markets last?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US inflation figures on Tuesday at 7:30 AM CT, and any news on US–Iran talks, which decide whether safe-haven money returns to the franc. No major Swiss data is scheduled. The next Swiss National Bank decision is December 10.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The Aussie held near 69.2 US cents. China bought far more from abroad than expected in October, which helps Australian exporters, but Australian consumer confidence fell to a four-year low.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised rates to 4.85% on November 3, the highest since 2008, but three members wanted to wait and Governor Michele Bullock hinted at a pause. A slump in AI and chip stocks pushed the Aussie to its lowest since March last week, before Monday's rebound. What changed: China's imports jumped about 42% on a year earlier in October, far above the 32% expected, while exports beat forecasts too. At home, the Westpac consumer confidence survey fell to its lowest since late 2022, with mortgage holders the gloomiest on record. What it means: Firmer Chinese buying is good news for Australia's exports, while gloomy households make another rate hike harder to justify. The two roughly cancelled out, leaving the Aussie trading on the mood in stock markets. The question: do stocks stay calm through today's US inflation figures?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US inflation figures on Tuesday at 7:30 AM CT; Australian jobs figures for October next Wednesday at 6:30 PM CT; and the next Reserve Bank of Australia decision on December 8.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The loonie slipped slightly, with the US dollar near 1.412 Canadian dollars, as US crude fell toward $86. The Bank of Canada publishes a summary of its October rate discussions at 12:30 PM CT.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Bank of Canada raised rates to 2.50% on October 28, its first hike since 2023, but Canada lost jobs in both September and October and unemployment rose to 6.7%, cutting bets on a December hike to about one in three. What changed: No Canadian news overnight. US crude settled almost 4.4% lower on Monday and slipped further in Asia as fears of new US strikes on Iran faded. What it means: Cheaper oil cuts what Canada earns from its biggest export, and with jobs weak, the case for another hike looks thinner. Today's summary will show how keen members were on more hikes. The question: does oil keep sliding as US–Iran talks move?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up, all times CT: Tuesday, 7:30 AM, US inflation figures; Tuesday, 12:30 PM, the Bank of Canada's summary of its October 28 discussions. Oil prices, which hinge on the US–Iran talks, also matter. The next Bank of Canada decision is December 9.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The kiwi held near 56.2 US cents after Monday's 1.6% jump, the biggest among major currencies. Strong Chinese demand for imports is mild good news for New Zealand's food exports.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand surprised by holding rates at 2.75% on October 28, and unemployment then rose to 5.7%, the highest since 2015, which cut bets on a December hike to below even. Saturday's election count pointed to Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's bloc keeping a narrow majority, and the kiwi jumped on Monday. What changed: No New Zealand news overnight. China's imports rose far more than expected in October, and the kiwi kept Monday's gain. What it means: Lower political risk and calmer stocks lifted the kiwi from a low base, and firmer Chinese demand helps at the margin. The rate story has not changed, so the bounce still rests on mood. The question: do stocks stay calm through today's US inflation figures?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US inflation figures on Tuesday at 7:30 AM CT; the official election result on November 27; and the next Reserve Bank of New Zealand decision on December 9.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Brent crude slipped toward $91 a barrel in Asia after falling almost 6% on Monday to its lowest since late August. President Donald Trump said he would hold off on new strikes on Iran but keep the US naval blockade.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The US–Iran war has kept the Strait of Hormuz, the route for about a fifth of the world's oil, mostly shut, and Brent ended October above $116. Hopes of a deal knocked it down about 16% last week. What changed: Brent settled at $92.57 on Monday, down 5.85%, after Trump said he would hold off on new strikes after appeals from Gulf states including Qatar, and it eased again in Asia. Gulf producers are cutting selling prices to win buyers as some ships move through Hormuz again, and OPEC pumped more in October, though attacks on ships near the strait continue. What it means: The war premium is draining out of the price before any deal is signed, and signs of plentiful supply add to the drop. That eases inflation worries for importers like Japan and the euro area and takes support from the Canadian dollar. The question: is the strait reopening for good, or will a new attack reverse the drop?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US inflation figures on Tuesday at 7:30 AM CT, which can move oil through the dollar; OPEC's monthly report on Wednesday; and any US answer to the Iranian offer or new attacks on shipping.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold eased slightly to near $4,113 an ounce in Asia, keeping most of Monday's gain as traders waited for US inflation figures. A hot reading would raise Fed hike bets, which tends to weigh on gold.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Iran war and high inflation have kept demand for gold strong, while rising interest rates hold it back; it hit a one-year low near $3,880 on October 30. On Monday it rose about 1.4% to near $4,125, winning back all of last Friday's loss after the US jobs report. What changed: Gold drifted a little lower in Asia as the dollar steadied and oil kept falling. What it means: Cheaper oil makes the inflation outlook less scary, which has helped gold, but bets on a December Fed hike remain high. That leaves gold exposed if US prices run hot, since higher rates raise the cost of holding a metal that pays no interest. The question: are real interest rates rising or falling after today's figures?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US inflation figures on Tuesday at 7:30 AM CT, which shape Fed hike bets and with them gold; Wednesday's US bond-market closure for Veterans Day, which can thin out trading; and US wholesale prices on Friday at 7:30 AM CT.

calls.text: Brent near $104.6 after Iran’s tanker-mine claim: with no US strike and no deal it stays between $100 and $110 by Thursday’s settlement; a new US strike sends it above $110
calls.note: Brent fell below the range, to about $94.6 on Wednesday and near $97.9 late Thursday.

calls.text: Euro near $1.118 before euro-area October inflation at 4:00 AM CT Wednesday: 4.0% or more keeps it above $1.115 by Wednesday’s close; 3.7% or less sends it below $1.112
calls.note: Inflation came in at 4.0% and the euro ended near $1.1236, above $1.115.

calls.text: Dollar near 158.5 yen after US yields rose: it stays between 157.0 and 159.5 yen by Wednesday’s close unless the ISM services survey beats its 54.9 forecast clearly, which lifts it above 159.5
calls.note: The ISM survey missed slightly and the dollar ended near 158.3 yen, inside the range.

calls.text: Gold near $3,955 after two straight gains: it stays between $3,880 and $4,030 by Wednesday’s close unless the ISM services survey beats clearly, which sends it below $3,880
calls.note: Gold broke out above the range, to about $4,059, as the dollar slid on the midterm results.

calls.text: US dollar near 1.399 loonies before Canada’s budget on Thursday: it stays between 1.392 and 1.406 by Thursday’s close unless Brent falls below $100, which lifts it above 1.406
calls.note: The US dollar ended near 1.399 loonies, inside the range.

calls.text: Aussie near 69.8 US cents after the split Reserve Bank of Australia hike: it stays between 69.2 and 70.5 cents by Wednesday’s close unless the yuan weakens further, which sends it below 69.2 cents
calls.note: The yuan steadied and the Aussie ended near 70.1 cents, inside the range.

calls.text: Dollar index near 101.8 on US midterm election day: it stays between 101.3 and 102.3 by Wednesday’s close unless the ISM services survey beats its 54.9 forecast clearly, which lifts it above 102.3
calls.note: The index fell to a one-month low but ended near 101.41, just inside the range.

calls.text: Dollar near 0.819 francs before Swiss October inflation at 1:30 AM CT Tuesday: a reading below the 0.0% forecast lifts it above 0.825 francs by Wednesday’s close; a reading above it keeps it below 0.819
calls.note: Inflation beat (1.5% against 1.3%) and the dollar ended near 0.816 francs, below 0.819.

calls.text: Kiwi near 56.2 US cents before New Zealand job figures at 3:45 PM CT Tuesday: unemployment of 5.4% or lower lifts it above 56.8 cents by Wednesday's close; 5.7% or higher sends it below 55.6 cents
calls.note: Unemployment hit 5.7%, but the kiwi only dipped to about 55.9 and ended near 56.3 cents, above 55.6.

calls.text: Brent near $104.80 after a 7.6% drop on Iran's backing for peace talks: with no US answer to the Doha draft and no strike, it stays between $100 and $110 by Wednesday's settlement; a US strike after the midterms sends it above $110
calls.note: With no US answer and no strike, Brent still fell to about $94.29, far below $100, on bets the war winds down.

calls.text: Dollar index near 101.7 before the US midterms and the ISM services survey at 9:00 AM CT Wednesday: it stays between 101.2 and 102.2 by Wednesday's close unless oil falls below $100 Brent, which sends it below 101.2
calls.note: Brent did fall below $100, but the index ended near 101.41, inside the range rather than below 101.2.

calls.text: Aussie near 70.2 US cents before the Reserve Bank of Australia decision at 9:30 PM CT Monday: a hike with a hint of more lifts it above 70.6 cents by Tuesday's close; a hold sends it below 69.5 cents
calls.note: The bank did hike, but with no hint of more; the Aussie ended Tuesday near 69.9 cents, neither above 70.6 nor below 69.5.

calls.text: Brent near $110 with Doha talks in a third day: with no deal and no US strike it stays between $105 and $115 by Tuesday's settlement; an agreed Hormuz reopening plan sends it below $105
calls.note: Brent ended Tuesday near $104.7, just below $105, without any agreed plan to reopen Hormuz.

calls.text: Dollar index near 101.6 after Fed officials Lorie Logan and Alberto Musalem called for more hikes: it stays between 101.2 and 102.1 by Monday's close unless the tech share slide deepens, which sends it below 101.2
calls.note: The dollar index ended Monday near 101.7, inside the range, even after a dip to about 101.4.

calls.text: Gold near $3,880 at a one-year low: it stays below $3,960 by Monday's close unless bets on a December Fed hike fall well below 70%
calls.note: Gold rose to about $3,941 but stayed below $3,960 at the close, with December hike bets near three in four.

calls.text: Loonie near 1.395 per US dollar after flat Canadian growth: with Brent above $111 the US dollar stays below 1.402 by Monday's close; Brent below $111 lifts it above 1.402
calls.note: Brent fell far below $111, to about $104.80, yet the US dollar stayed near 1.397 loonies, below 1.402, as trade-deal hopes cushioned the loonie.

calls.text: Euro near $1.117 before euro-area October inflation at 4:00 AM CT Wednesday: 3.8% or more keeps it above $1.112 by Wednesday's close; 3.5% or less sends it below $1.110
calls.note: Inflation came in at 4.0% and the euro ended near $1.1236, above $1.112.

calls.text: Pound near $1.340 before the Bank of England at 6:00 AM CT Thursday, November 5: a hike with a hint of more keeps it above $1.333 by Thursday's close; a hike framed as the last sends it below $1.333
calls.note: The hike came with a hint of more, and the pound ended near $1.347, above $1.333.

calls.text: Dollar index near 101.8 before the US Employment Cost Index at 7:30 AM CT Friday: wage costs of 0.9% or more for the quarter lift it back above 102.2 by Friday's close; 0.7% or less keeps it below 101.8
calls.note: Neither branch: wage costs rose exactly 0.8%, as forecast. The index still ended near 101.6, as a tech share slide pulled US yields lower.

calls.text: Gold near $3,996 before US wage figures at 7:30 AM CT Friday: wage costs at or above forecast keep it below $4,060 by Friday's close; a soft reading lifts it above $4,060
calls.note: Wage costs matched the forecast and gold fell to about $3,882, far below $4,060.

calls.text: Dollar near ¥158 before Tokyo inflation figures and the Bank of Japan decision overnight: it stays between ¥157 and ¥159 by Friday's close unless Governor Kazuo Ueda clearly signals a December hike, which sends it below ¥157
calls.note: Governor Kazuo Ueda gave no clear December signal, and the dollar ended near ¥157.5, inside the range.

calls.text: Euro near $1.116 before euro-area October inflation at 5:00 AM CT Friday: inflation at or above 3.8% keeps it above $1.112 by Friday's close; a reading of 3.5% or less sends it below $1.110
calls.note: The premise broke: the euro-area inflation figure is due Wednesday, November 4, not Friday. The euro still held above $1.112, near $1.117.

calls.text: Aussie near 70.3 US cents with a November 3 Reserve Bank of Australia hike mostly priced: a hike keeps it above 70 cents by Tuesday's close; a hold sends it below 69.5 cents
calls.note: The hike came, but the Aussie ended Tuesday near 69.9 cents, below 70, as the governor gave no hint of more.

calls.text: Brent near $114 before the OPEC+ meeting on Sunday: with no formal US–Iran talks it stays between $110 and $118 by Monday's settlement; formal talks send it below $110
calls.note: Brent fell below $110, to about $104.80 at Monday's settlement, without formal US–Iran talks; indirect talks through Qatar and Iran's backing for diplomacy did the work.

calls.text: Loonie near 1.398 per US dollar after the Bank of Canada hike: the US dollar stays below 1.405 by Friday's close unless Canada's August GDP at 7:30 AM CT Friday disappoints
calls.note: Canada's August growth did disappoint (flat against +0.2%), yet the US dollar fell to about 1.395 loonies as oil rose and the US dollar weakened broadly.

calls.text: Gold near $4,040 before US PCE inflation at 7:30 AM CT Thursday: core PCE above 0.3% on the month keeps it below $4,050 by Thursday's close; 0.2% or less lifts it above $4,075
calls.note: Neither branch: core PCE rose exactly 0.3%. Gold fell to about $4,025, below $4,050.

calls.text: Dollar index near 102.05 before US growth and PCE inflation figures at 7:30 AM CT Thursday: core PCE above 0.3% on the month lifts it above 102.4 by Thursday's close; 0.2% or less pulls it below 101.7
calls.note: Neither branch: core PCE rose exactly 0.3%. The dollar index ended near 102.15, between the two levels.

calls.text: Euro near $1.116 before the European Central Bank at 8:15 AM CT Thursday: a hold with a clear December hike signal keeps it above $1.112 by Thursday's close; a vague December message sends it below $1.112
calls.note: Lagarde said a hike was discussed and the euro closed near $1.116, above $1.112, after an early dip to about $1.111.

calls.text: Dollar near ¥157.8 before Tokyo inflation figures at 6:30 PM CT tonight: it stays between ¥157 and ¥158.5 by Thursday's close unless Tokyo prices surprise sharply
calls.note: The dollar ended near ¥157.97, inside the range; Tokyo prices are still to come tonight.

calls.text: Brent near $115.7 with no confirmed Ras Tanura damage: it stays between $112 and $119 by Thursday's settlement; confirmed damage or a US strike signal sends it above $119
calls.note: No damage was confirmed and Brent stayed inside the range, near $113.8 at the last verified quote.

calls.text: Kiwi near 56.1 US cents after the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's surprise hold: a firm Fed at 1:00 PM CT keeps it below 56.5 by Wednesday's close; a softer Fed lets it recover toward 56.8
calls.note: The Fed sounded softer than feared, but Blue Street has no verified kiwi level after the decision; the last check was near 56.1 cents.

calls.text: Aussie near 70.35 US cents with a November RBA hike about 80% priced: it holds above 70 by Wednesday's close unless a firm Fed lifts the US dollar broadly
calls.note: The Aussie held above 70 cents and rose to a five-week high near 70.6.

calls.text: Brent near $115 as Saudi Arabia stays silent on Ras Tanura: with no confirmed damage it stays between $112 and $118 by Wednesday's settlement; confirmed damage sends it above $118
calls.note: No damage was confirmed and Brent stayed inside the range, near $115.7 at the last verified quote.

calls.text: Dollar index near 102.3 before the Fed decision at 1:00 PM CT Wednesday: if Fed chair Kevin Warsh keeps a December hike clearly on the table, it holds above 102 by Wednesday's close; if he plays it down, it slips toward 101.7
calls.note: Warsh did not tie himself to December, yet December hike pricing rose to about 86%; the index slipped to about 102.05, just above 102.

calls.text: Pound near $1.331 before the UK Budget at about 7:30 AM CT Wednesday: modest extra borrowing keeps it between $1.325 and $1.338 by Wednesday's close; borrowing well above expectations sends it below $1.325
calls.note: The Budget was calm; the pound dipped to about $1.327 and ended near $1.334, inside the range.

calls.text: US dollar near 1.403 Canadian before the Bank of Canada at 8:45 AM CT Wednesday: a hike with a signal of more pushes it below 1.398; a hold lifts it above 1.41
calls.note: The bank hiked and said more may be needed, but the US dollar only eased to about 1.4035 Canadian, not below 1.398.

calls.text: Dollar index near 102.0 before US durable goods (7:30 AM CT) and consumer confidence (9:00 AM CT): firm readings keep it at or above 102 by Tuesday's close; weak ones pull it toward 101.7
calls.note: Durable goods, consumer confidence and new home sales all beat, and the dollar index closed near 102.3.

calls.text: Brent near $115 as talks with Iran continue: with no deal and no confirmed hit on Saudi output, it stays between $112 and $118 by Tuesday's settlement; a confirmed hit sends it above $118
calls.note: The Houthi claim on Ras Tanura was not confirmed and the talks continued; Brent ended near $114.80, inside the range.

calls.text: Dollar near ¥157.5 before Japan's services prices tonight and US data Tuesday: firm US figures keep it between ¥157 and ¥158 by Tuesday's close; a stock sell-off pulls it below ¥157
calls.note: US figures were firm and stocks rose; the dollar ended near ¥157.8, inside the range.

calls.text: Kiwi near 56.8 US cents before the Reserve Bank of New Zealand decision at 8:00 PM CT Tuesday: a hike with a signal of more lifts it above 57.2 cents; a hike framed as the last sends it below 56.5
calls.note: The premise broke: the bank held instead of hiking. The kiwi still fell below 56.5 cents, to about 55.8 at the low and near 56.1 in Asia.

calls.text: Aussie near 70.2 US cents before Australia's third-quarter inflation figures at 7:30 PM CT Tuesday: a trimmed mean above 1.0% on the quarter lifts it above 70.5 cents; 0.8% or less pulls it below 70
calls.note: Neither branch: the trimmed mean rose exactly 1.0%, though above the bank's own forecast. The Aussie briefly topped 70.5 cents, then settled near 70.35.

calls.text: Brent near $110 on the Tehran peace efforts: a confirmed attack on Saudi oil sites or a breakdown in talks sends it back above $115 by the close; no news lets it hold between $105 and $112
calls.note: Brent was never near $110 at the settlement: it ended down 0.8% at about $115.81, with no attack and no breakdown in talks; early reports of a 6% fall did not hold up.

calls.text: Dollar index near 101.7 with no major US data left today: if oil keeps falling, it slips toward 101.5 by the close; an oil rebound lifts it back toward 101.8
calls.note: Oil eased only slightly, yet the dollar index rose to about 102.0 by the close, past both levels, as investors favoured the dollar before the Fed.

calls.text: Pound near $1.337 before Wednesday's UK Budget: with no UK data, it stays between $1.333 and $1.341 by the close; a Budget leak on borrowing moves it out of that range
calls.note: With no UK data and no Budget leak, the pound ended near $1.3346, inside the range.

calls.text: Brent near $114 after Aramco cleared its Dhahran headquarters: a Houthi hit that cuts Saudi output lifts Brent past its May highs and supports the loonie; a quiet weekend lets it ease toward $110
calls.note: Both happened in turn: Houthi attacks lifted Brent to about $117 on Friday without a confirmed cut to Saudi output, then a quiet weekend and talks in Tehran took it to about $110 by Monday.

calls.text: Canada retail sales Fri 7:30 AM CT (about +1.3% expected for August): a strong rebound lifts bets on Bank of Canada hikes beyond October 28; a miss keeps it to one
calls.note: Sales rose 1.2%, a touch under the 1.3% expected, so neither a strong beat nor a miss; Bank of Canada hike pricing for October 28 stayed near 75–80%.

calls.text: Brent near $112 after the Iran strike-plan report: a confirmed hit on Gulf oil output or a US move toward strikes pushes it above the $112.68 high and lifts the yen and franc; an official denial lets it slip toward $108 by the close
calls.note: Brent did top the high, to about $113, and the yen and franc gained, but without a confirmed hit or an official US move: the report alone and Iran's tanker claims did it.

calls.text: Euro-area consumer confidence 9:00 AM CT (about −17 expected) with France's gap over Germany at its widest since 2011: a weaker reading keeps the euro under $1.12; a steady one lets it recover
calls.note: The reading was weaker (−17.9), yet the euro recovered to about $1.1218 as US yields fell, so the bond rally outweighed the survey.

calls.text: US bond rally on war fears: if the 10-year yield stays near 5.05% into the close, the yen holds its gains near ¥157; if yields rebound on the strong claims figure, the dollar climbs back toward ¥158
calls.note: Yields did not rebound; they fell further, to about 4.95%, on a tech sell-off, and the yen extended its gains to about ¥156.85.

calls.text: US 10-year yield below 5% after the tech sell-off: if Asian and European stocks keep falling overnight, the yen pushes toward ¥156 and the dollar index slips under 101.5; a rebound in stocks lifts yields and the dollar back toward ¥157.5
calls.note: Asian stocks kept falling (Nikkei −1.3%) and the dollar dipped to about ¥156.3, but steadied near ¥156.9 by 12:40 AM CT; the dollar index held at about 101.5 rather than slipping under it.

calls.text: Euro-area flash business surveys Fri 3:00 AM CT (manufacturing ~52.7, services ~52.6 expected), hours before Moody's on France: misses keep the euro near $1.12; beats firm December ECB hike bets and lift it
calls.note: The surveys missed (euro-area composite 51.9, France back in contraction at 48.4), and the euro stayed near $1.12.

calls.text: US flash PMIs Fri 8:45 AM CT (services ~58.0 expected) and Michigan inflation expectations 9:00 AM CT: firm readings lift yields back toward 5% and steady the dollar; soft ones extend the bond rally
calls.note: The surveys were firm on prices and the Michigan inflation outlook ticked up; the 10-year yield rose back to about 5.00% and the dollar index firmed to about 101.8 on Friday.

calls.text: SNB policy summary 2:30 AM CT: worry about a strong franc keeps December cut bets alive and caps the franc; a calmer tone lets it firm
calls.note: Calmer tone: the bank dropped its stronger readiness to intervene and gave no December cut signal. The franc firmed slightly, with the dollar near 0.823, and hit a three-month high against the euro.

calls.text: Saudi departure order: widening across the Gulf or a hit on Saudi output puts Brent well above $110 and lifts the dollar and loonie; staying contained lets oil drift
calls.note: Brent did climb well above $110 (about $113 by the close), but on reports of US–Israeli strike plans and Iranian tanker claims, not a wider departure order. The loonie edged up; the dollar slipped.

calls.text: UK retail sales Fri 1:00 AM CT (−0.2% expected): a strong print lifts December hike bets and the pound; a weak one trims both
calls.note: Sales fell 0.4%, worse than expected, yet the pound reached its strongest against the euro since May 2025 on Friday as a November Bank of England hike stayed near certain.

calls.text: US jobless claims Thu 7:30 AM CT (about 200,000 expected): staying low keeps the Fed's December hike near 90%; a jump trims it and weighs on the dollar
calls.note: Claims stayed low at 194,000 (200,000 expected), near their lowest in decades. December hike bets held near 90% (CME FedWatch, Oct 21); a sharp bond rally later still pulled the dollar lower.

calls.text: Moody's review of France Fri: a downgrade widens France's gap over German yields and weighs on the euro; holding the rating eases the pressure
calls.note: Moody's held France at Aa3; French yields eased on Monday and the euro led the majors in the European morning.

calls.text: Bailey 8:00 AM CT after the 3.5% UK inflation print: backing November without promising more keeps the pound near $1.34; any opening to a December follow-up lifts it; calling energy temporary trims it
calls.note: Neither branch: Bailey gave no new signal on rates. The pound still held near $1.34 (about 1.3395 at the New York close), with December's second hike about a coin toss.

calls.text: US crude oil stocks 9:30 AM CT (industry survey: about −4.9M barrels): a big official draw keeps Brent above $110; a build lets the rebound fade
calls.note: The draw came (−3.1M barrels, far more than forecast) and Brent briefly topped $110.8, but it still faded to $108.82 at the settle after the US Treasury's tanker licence and emergency fuel loans.

calls.text: Pakistan's mediation after Iran's uranium refusal: any confirmed opening drains oil's premium and lifts the euro and yen; more warships and no talks keep Brent near $110 into the close
calls.note: No opening: Rubio called a deal extremely difficult and more US warships headed in. Brent settled at $108.82, near $110 but off its high on Washington's supply moves rather than diplomacy.

calls.text: Japan national CPI Thu 6:30 PM CT (2.1% expected): a hot print keeps the BoJ's December hike near three in four; a soft one fades it and weighs on the yen
calls.note: Neither branch: 2.1% exactly as expected (1.7% prior), though the measure that also leaves out energy jumped to 2.4%. December hike pricing held near 80%.

calls.text: US–Iran framework: confirmation by either government drains oil's risk premium and pulls US long yields lower; another denial puts Brent back toward $110
calls.note: No confirmation from either government, and no fresh denial either. Brent still climbed back toward $110 overnight, on tanker attacks spreading to the Gulf of Oman rather than on the talks.

calls.text: RBA's Hauser 5:30 PM CT: leaning on sticky inflation keeps a November hike near 1 in 3; leaning on the softer job market trims it
calls.note: Hauser leaned on sticky inflation: the outlook is 'materially worse'. Odds of a November hike rose to about 40% from about 30%, and the Aussie hit a three-week high near 0.702.

calls.text: China Q3 GDP 4.5% vs 4.4% fc — the aussie's demand read
calls.note: Beat: 4.5% vs 4.4% fc (q/q 1.2%); retail +1.1% the standout. AUD/USD +0.3-0.5% to ~0.697, the night's best G10 performer; USD/CNH 6.6811, strongest since June 2022. Two-speed beat (factories lead, property -20.6% YTD).

calls.text: Petersburg Oil Terminal drone strike — Baltic supply risk into Monday's open vs the waiver's lower-price pull
calls.note: Fire CONFIRMED (Beglov; Fire Point confirmed its FP-1 hit the terminal); ~1 killed, several injured (figures vary); damage extent still unquantified. Crude's Sunday open came flat — neither the spike nor the tumble; Asia Brent -1.0 to -1.8%.

calls.text: Beirut strike fallout: the haven-bid tell at Monday's open
calls.note: No Hezbollah retaliation as of Monday's open (Qmati: strike crossed a 'red line', leadership to decide; IDF: normal routines). Haven bid stayed sheathed — DXY flat 101.80-101.83, havens ~flat in Asia. The tell held: no escalation, no haven extension.

calls.text: October FOMC priced as a hold (~85%) into the Saturday blackout; December is the live debate
Brent broke $108 on Ukraine refinery strikes — $105-112 range into the weekend (prior $104-108 call broken)
USD/CAD holds 1.41-1.43 into the BoC (Oct 28); Canada CPI Mon the trigger
calls.note: Oct 19: CPI passed without a break — USD/CAD ~1.411 at the NY close, still inside the range. Runs to the Oct 28 decision. Oct 20: dipped to ~1.409, a hair under the floor, as oil and BoC hike bets lifted the loonie. Oct 20 close: broke below the floor — USD/CAD ~1.406, strongest loonie since Sep 22, on BoC hike pricing (~80–85%) and Alberta's vote to remain.
The tripwire never bit — Friday's waiver suspends the duties outright with no end date. Superseded by the ~Dec 17 60-day review clock.
calls.text: Graham Act Oct-18 tripwire: waivers extended or enforcement begins — oil's Sunday open is the tell
Iran deal Sunday signing: Trump's 'OPEN TO ALL' vs Tehran's 'not tomorrow' — the strait itself is the verdict
calls.note: No signed deal carried by any major wire by 4pm CT Sunday; Trump's 'complete' claim stands unverified against Tehran's 'talks stalled'. Aggregator 'markets celebrate' content held — its futures numbers contradict Friday's verified settles. The signing test is claim day, not done day.

calls.text: Canada CPI Mon 7:30am CT (TD 3.2%, UBS 3.3%, RBC 3.0%): hot (3.3%+) revives the Oct 28 hike; soft (3.0%-) buries it to December
calls.note: Neither branch: 3.1% vs 3.2% expected, core measures cooled to 1.8–1.9%. October stayed about 1 in 4 (a hold), with about one quarter-point hike priced by December; consumers' inflation expectations rose to ~3.9% in the BoC survey. Correction (Oct 20): by Monday's close swaps had jumped to ~87% for an October hike on Macklem's Saturday forecast warning; the 1-in-4 figure was stale.

calls.text: UK CPI Wed 1am CT (3.4% fc vs 3.1%): 3.5%+ starts pricing a December follow-up; soft reopens Bailey's 2027 read
calls.note: Hot branch: 3.5% vs 3.4% expected (3.1% in August), the highest in 11 months. November's hike is near certain; how much December moved was not yet verified at write.

calls.text: NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (ANZ 3.8% y/y): hot settles the RBNZ's two-way bet toward the hike side
calls.note: Not hot: inflation came in at 3.7%, a touch soft. The hike side still settled anyway, with October 28 now about 98% priced.

calls.text: Japan CPI Fri + BoJ Oct 29-30: Ueda's 'quite close' language tested — October hike stays ~25%
calls.note: Oct 19: swaps now put an October 30 hike under 5% (BBH), below the ~25% in the call. December ~80% unchanged. October hike odds fell to about 4%, far below the ~25% in the call; Japan's inflation came in at 2.1% as expected and December (~80%) is now the meeting that matters.

calls.text: France's revenue-section budget vote Tue: a clean pass narrows the French–German spread (~141bp); a defeat or big concessions widens it and weighs on the euro
calls.note: No vote on Tuesday: it was pushed to October 27, so neither branch played out.

calls.text: UK jobs Tue 1 AM CT (earnings ~3.8% expected): sticky pay firms the BoE hike case before Wednesday's inflation; cooling pay backs Bailey's calmer view
calls.note: Sticky side won: unemployment fell to 4.7% (4.9% expected) and regular pay rose 3.7% (3.6% expected); total pay and claims were softer. Pound +0.3% to ~1.334.

calls.text: Konarak follow-through: a US confirmation or more strikes keeps oil's supply premium and lifts US yields; silence lets the morning's waiver drop resume
calls.note: No confirmation (a US official denied the strike) and no new strike overnight, yet the premium held: Brent ~$109.8 Tuesday on low Gulf flows and Iran's Hormuz claims. The waiver-driven drop did not resume.

calls.text: BoC Oct 28 with ~87% priced for a hike: a hike is mostly in the loonie already; a hold would be the surprise and hit it
calls.note: The Bank of Canada hiked as priced, and the loonie barely moved on the day.

calls.text: NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (~3.8% y/y): near forecast keeps the ~80% hike pricing; clearly soft reopens the hold and weighs on the kiwi
calls.note: Near forecast (3.7% vs 3.8%) and hike pricing held, rising to about 98%; the kiwi dipped only briefly.
